title: world_directory/2 — GET /worlds: the worlds a caller may choose between (SPEC-028). A DIRECTORY, never canon: an id, a name, a line of fiction, a look, a cover, where you left off, and whether anyone can play it. No world STATE on this surface.

display_name.description: The world's name as a chooser sees it. The one label in the system that is not viewer-relative, because it names the CONTAINER rather than anything inside it — B-1 governs what is in a world.

tagline.description: ONE world-authored line selling the world on its card. AUTHORED FICTION (GA-2): this service never composes it — no default, no template. null when the world's author has not written one, and the card renders without it. Never an empty string; a blank is rejected at the column.

playable.description: Whether this world states a player (world.player_entity_id). False for a world created through POST /worlds that has nothing authored into it yet — real, listed, and not yet enterable.

cover_image.description: The world's cover art. Image reference, or null when there is no picture yet — the ordinary state, and what the frontend's placeholder is for. It swaps in on a later read with no re-request and no subscription. Carries an asset id and a PATH back to the world backend, never a presigned URL: those expire (~15 min), so an embedded one would make this payload rot in any cache or log. Fetch as {apiBase}{path}, optionally ?tier=thumbnail|preview|final (256/768/1024, default preview); the backend mints a fresh short-lived URL per read and redirects.

last_place_label.description: The world's own label for where its player stands, or left off. A LABEL AND NOTHING ELSE — no tick, no timestamp, no '2 hours ago' (B-5 keeps wall-clock off this boundary, and a directory is a shelf of doors, not a save-game list). Rendered as the world's player, whose whereabouts it is and who a caller becomes on entering. null when the world has no player yet, or has one who has never been placed anywhere — never entered, nothing to say.

world_theme.description: SPEC-019 theme tokens. ONE accent colour — the frontend derives the rest, because a backend shipping a palette would own visual design it has no business owning. mood is an ATMOSPHERE word, never a genre: the system never learns the word 'fantasy' (GA-3).

mood.description: Draft vocabulary: daylight | nocturne | mist | ember | bleak. Deliberately NOT constrained to that set — unknown values must DEGRADE in the client, never fail here. Enforcing the enum backend-side would make this service the thing that breaks on a word it has not heard of, which is backwards for a field whose purpose is to evolve.

ornament.description: Draft vocabulary: none | filigree | rivet | vine | circuit. Unconstrained for the same reason as mood.
